## Introduction

This document presents the results of the impact of the adoption of cosy tariff on smart meter electricity consumption at the household level.

Done:

- Add weather [done - but using reanalysis data, the MET data from databricks only starts in 2022]: I decided to use GSP* date trends instead
- Implement Callaway and sant'anna DiD [done but more work needed on the panel balance]: I have settled on almost a year but could restrict further
- Decide of a threshold for the event study (how many weeks before / after adoption we want to capture, do we want to put all weeks before in a large category or exclude them)

To do: 

- Can we find out when they install their HP
- heterogeneity: epc data, what tariff they were on before
- calculate price elasticities
- calculate emissions savings



```{r download-data}

aggregated_data <- fread("data/input/Cosy Cal.csv") %>%
  rename(total_consumption = total_read_value,
         tariff_gsp_group_id = gsp) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(settlement_date),
         is_on_cosy = ifelse(pre_post_cosy=="post", 1, 0)
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(settlement_date, pre_post_cosy))


# Define the start date from which to count weeks
start_date <- min(aggregated_data$date, na.rm = TRUE)

adoption <- aggregated_data %>%
  group_by(mpan, is_on_cosy) %>%
  arrange(mpan, is_on_cosy, date) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  filter(is_on_cosy==1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(mpan, date) %>%
  rename(adoption = date) %>%
  mutate(
    firstweek = floor_date(adoption, "week")
  )

did_data <- aggregated_data %>%
  inner_join(adoption) %>%
  mutate(weeks_since_cosy = floor(as.numeric(difftime(date, adoption, units = "weeks")))) %>%
  group_by(mpan, date)  %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate the difference in weeks from the start_date
    week = as.numeric(difftime(date, start_date, units = "weeks")) %/% 1 + 1,
    # Assuming you have a way to determine 'firstweek', adjust similarly if needed
    firstweek = as.numeric(difftime(firstweek, start_date, units = "weeks")) %/% 1 + 1) %>%
  group_by(mpan, firstweek, weeks_since_cosy, week, tariff_gsp_group_id, rate_period) %>%
  summarise(total_consumption = sum(total_consumption)) %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.numeric(mpan),
    firstweek = as.numeric(firstweek),
    week = as.numeric(week), 
    is_on_cosy = ifelse(firstweek<=week, 1, 0)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(week)) %>%
  group_by(mpan, week) %>%
  mutate(weekly_consumption = sum(total_consumption),
         share_consumption = total_consumption/weekly_consumption) 


weather <- fread("data/input/Cosy Analysis Weather Mar 26.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate the difference in weeks from the start_date
    week = as.numeric(difftime(week_start, start_date, units = "weeks")) %/% 1 + 1)

did_data <- did_data %>%
  left_join(weather, by=c("week", "tariff_gsp_group_id" = "gsp_group_id")) 

did_data <- did_data %>%
  mutate(month = month(week_start))

rm(aggregated_data)
```

## Difference in differences

We run the following model by period and on total daily consumption for all customers that have adopted Cosy in the past year: 

$$Consumption_{it} = \alpha OnCosy_{it} + \delta_t +  \gamma_i + GSP \times \delta_t+  \epsilon_{it} $$
with:

- $Consumption_{it}$ - electricty consumption in kWh (column 1) and log (column 2) for customer $i$ on day $t$ 
- $OnCosy_{it}$ a dummy variable equals 1 if the customer has switched to Cosy, 0 otherwise. To be noted: right now, adoption is permanent, I am not switching back to 0 for people that switched to another tariff
- $\delta_t$, $\gamma_i$, $ GSP \times \delta_t$ are day $t$,  customer $i$, and GSP regions times day fixed effects
The standard errors are clustered at the customer (MPAN) level. 

### Consumption by period

```{r, did-period, include=TRUE}

m1 <- feols(total_consumption ~ as.factor(is_on_cosy) | week + mpan + week^tariff_gsp_group_id,
            data = did_data,
            cluster = ~mpan,
            split = ~ rate_period)
m2 <- feols(weekly_consumption ~ as.factor(is_on_cosy) | week + mpan + week^tariff_gsp_group_id,
            data = did_data %>% select(mpan, week, is_on_cosy, tariff_gsp_group_id, weekly_consumption) %>% distinct(),
            cluster = ~mpan)

did <- etable(m1, m2)

did

rm(did)


```


### Share electricity consumption

We repeat the same analysis on share of daily consumption by period. 

```{r, did-daily-total, include=TRUE}

m1 <- feols(share_consumption ~ as.factor(is_on_cosy) | week + mpan + week^tariff_gsp_group_id, 
            data = did_data, 
            cluster = ~mpan, 
            split = ~ rate_period)

did <- etable(m1)

did

rm(did)

```

## Event study

We run the following model by period for all customers that have adopted Cosy in the past year: 

$$Consumption_{it} = \sum^W _{w={-52, -9, ..., 1, ..,52}} \alpha_w WeeksSinceCosy^w_{it} + X\beta + \delta_t +  \gamma_i +  \epsilon_{it} $$
where:
- $WeeksSinceCosy^w_{it}$  is a categorical variable equals to the number of weeks before and after the adoption of Cosy. We use the week prior adoption as omitted category. 

### Consumption by period

```{r panelcheck}

# Calculating the first and last week of data for each mpan
mpan_weeks <- aggregated_data %>%
  group_by(mpan) %>%
  summarise(
    first_date = min(date),
    last_date = max(date),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    first_week = floor_date(first_date, "week"),
    last_week = floor_date(last_date, "week")
  )

# Creating a table by first and last week
week_table <- mpan_weeks %>%
  group_by(first_week, last_week) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Viewing the table
head(week_table)
table(aggregated_data$weeks_since_cosy)


```

```{r, event-study-period,  include=TRUE}

# Fixed-effects regression
est_did <- feols(total_consumption ~  i(weeks_since_cosy, -1) |  mpan + month, 
                 data = did_data %>% filter(weeks_since_cosy > -50,
                                            weeks_since_cosy < 50),
                 split =~ rate_period,
                 cluster = ~mpan)

m2 <- feols(weekly_consumption ~ i(weeks_since_cosy, -1) |  mpan + month,
            data = did_data %>% 
              filter(weeks_since_cosy > -50,
                                            weeks_since_cosy < 50)%>% 
              select(mpan, weeks_since_cosy, month, weekly_consumption) %>% distinct(),
            cluster = ~mpan)

# Now we can plot the result of the interaction with coefplot

coefplot(est_did[2], title="Effect on total consumption - Morning Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[1], title="Effect on total consumption - Afternoon Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[3], title="Effect on total consumption - Peak rate")
coefplot(est_did[4], title="Effect on total consumption - Other rate")
coefplot(m2, title="Effect on total consumption - Other rate")


```


```{r, event-study-period-share, eval=FALSE}

# Remove all objects except for 'aggregated_data'
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), "did_data"))
gc()

est_did <- feols(share_consumption ~ i(weeks_since_cosy, -1) |  mpan + month, 
                 data = did_data %>% filter(weeks_since_cosy > -50,
                                            weeks_since_cosy < 50,
                                            !is.na(share_consumption)),
                 split =~ rate_period,
                 cluster = ~mpan) 


# Now we can plot the result of the interaction with coefplot

coefplot(est_did[2], title="Effect on total consumption - Morning Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[1], title="Effect on total consumption - Afternoon Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[3], title="Effect on total consumption - Peak rate")
coefplot(est_did[4], title="Effect on total consumption - Other rate")

```

## Callaway Sant'Anna DiD

```{r, callsanta, include=TRUE}
# Getting unique rate periods to loop over
unique_periods <- unique(did_data$rate_period)

if (!file.exists("data/scratch/estimates_list.RDS")) { 
  
  # Initialize a list to store estimates for each period
  estimates_list <- list()
  
  for(period in unique_periods) {
    

    # Estimating the treatment effect using the Callaway and Sant'Anna method
    est_cs <- att_gt(yname = "total_consumption",
                     tname = "week",
                     idname = "id",
                     gname = "firstweek",
                     data = did_data,
                     control_group="notyettreated",
                     allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE)
    
    # agg
    agg.simple <- aggte(est_cs, type = "simple", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
    
    # event study style
    agg.es <- aggte(est_cs, type = "dynamic", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
    
    # by cohort
    agg.grp <- aggte(est_cs, type = "group", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
    
    # by season
    agg.cal <- aggte(MP = est_cs, type = "calendar",  na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
    
    # Store estimates in the list with period as the name
    estimates_list[[period]] <- list(simple = agg.simple, dynamic = agg.es, group = agg.grp, calendar = agg.cal)
    
  }
  
  
  # Adjust your existing code to calculate 'week' and 'firstweek' as the number of weeks from the start_date
  did_data <- aggregated_data %>%
    mutate(
      # Calculate the difference in weeks from the start_date
      week = as.numeric(difftime(date, start_date, units = "weeks")) %/% 1 + 1,
      # Assuming you have a way to determine 'firstweek', adjust similarly if needed
      firstweek = as.numeric(difftime(firstweek, start_date, units = "weeks")) %/% 1 + 1) %>%
    group_by(mpan, firstweek, week, tariff_gsp_group_id) %>%
    summarise(total_consumption = sum(total_consumption)) %>%
    mutate(
      id = as.numeric(mpan),
      firstweek = as.numeric(firstweek),
      week = as.numeric(week)
    )
  
  # Estimating the treatment effect using the Callaway and Sant'Anna method
  est_cs <- att_gt(yname = "total_consumption",
                   tname = "week",
                   idname = "id",
                   gname = "firstweek",
                   data = did_data,
                   control_group="notyettreated",
                   allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE)
  
  # agg
  agg.simple <- aggte(est_cs, type = "simple", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
  
  # event study style
  agg.es <- aggte(est_cs, type = "dynamic", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
  
  # by cohort
  agg.grp <- aggte(est_cs, type = "group", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
  
  # by season
  agg.cal <- aggte(MP = est_cs, type = "calendar",  na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id", min_e = -49, max_e=49, bstrap=TRUE)
  
  # Store estimates in the list with period as the name
  estimates_list[["Overall"]] <- list(simple = agg.simple, dynamic = agg.es, group = agg.grp, calendar = agg.cal)
  
  saveRDS(estimates_list, "data/scratch/estimates_list.RDS")
  
  
} else {
  estimates_list <- readRDS("data/scratch/estimates_list.RDS")
}

for(period in c(unique_periods, "Overall")) {
  
  print(paste("Aggregate effect for", period))
  print(summary(estimates_list[[period]]$simple))
  
  # Plotting for each period
  ggdid_title <- paste(period, "Effect")
  print(ggdid(estimates_list[[period]]$dynamic, title = ggdid_title))
  print(ggdid(estimates_list[[period]]$calendar, title = ggdid_title))
  print(ggdid(estimates_list[[period]]$group, title = ggdid_title))
  
} 
```
